description:
Spec commit `bb7ff59` (2026-05-02) added `ReadDisposition` to `Message` and `Peer/receipt` per draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §ReadDisposition (lines 305–318) and §Message/set update (line 1012). The catch-up landed in two of three places but not in chat-client:

| Crate | Status |
|---|---|
| `jmap-chat-types` | ✅ enum (`message.rs:42-53`) with values `Displayed`, `Deleted`, `Processed`, `Other(String)`; field on `Message` (`message.rs:235-237`) and `DeliveryReceipt` (`message.rs:305-307`); property selector variant; round-trip tests covering all 4 oracles. |
| `jmap-chat-server` | ✅ `handle_message_set` defaults missing `readDisposition` to `"displayed"` per spec §1012 when `readAt` is set without explicit disposition; integration tests at `tests/integration.rs:827-972` cover all 4 oracles. |
| `jmap-chat-client` | ❌ `MessageCreateInput` (`src/methods/mod.rs:383-399`) and `MessagePatch` (`src/methods/mod.rs:456-478`) have no `read_disposition` field. `message_create` (`src/methods/message.rs:163-203`) and `message_update` (`src/methods/message.rs:215-295`) have no passthrough. Typed callers cannot produce `"deleted"`, `"processed"`, or vendor disposition values — the server always falls through to its `"displayed"` default. |

## Scope

`crate-jmap-chat-client` only. No spec change needed (the spec already defines the field as settable on `update`). No `jmap-chat-types` or `jmap-chat-server` changes needed.

## Implementation sketch

1. **`MessagePatch`** (`src/methods/mod.rs:456-478`): add `pub read_disposition: Option<jmap_chat_types::ReadDisposition>` field. Keep `#[non_exhaustive]`. Document the spec §Message/set update semantics: setting `read_at` without `read_disposition` causes the server to store `"displayed"`; supplying both lets the client pick `"deleted"` or `"processed"` explicitly. Clients SHOULD only set `read_disposition` when they also set `read_at`.

2. **`message_update`** (`src/methods/message.rs:215-295`): add a passthrough hunk paralleling the existing `read_at` block, e.g.:

   ```rust
   if let Some(rd) = &patch.read_disposition {
       patch_map.insert(
           "readDisposition".into(),
           serde_json::to_value(rd)
               .map_err(|e| jmap_base_client::ClientError::Internal(e.to_string()))?,
       );
   }
   ```

3. **`MessageCreateInput`** (`src/methods/mod.rs:383-399`): the spec §Message/set is silent on `readDisposition` at create time (the field is described as `server-set`, and §1012 only documents it in the `update` context). Recommend: do NOT add `read_disposition` to `MessageCreateInput`. If a future deployment wants to pre-populate the disposition at create time, that's a wire-spec extension question, not a client-binding question. Confirm this interpretation in the bead's claim phase by re-reading §ReadDisposition (lines 305-318) and §Message (the per-property table that classifies the field as server-set).

4. **Re-export**: `jmap_chat_types::ReadDisposition` should be re-exported from `jmap-chat-client::lib.rs` so callers don't need a second `use` statement for it. Verify whether other types from `jmap-chat-types::message` are re-exported and follow the same pattern (or non-pattern).

## Tests

Add at least these unit tests to the chat-client `src/methods/message.rs` test module:

1. `message_update_with_read_disposition_displayed_serialises_correctly` — set `read_at` + `read_disposition: Displayed`, assert the emitted JMAP method-call payload's `update` map for that id contains both `"readAt"` and `"readDisposition": "displayed"`.

2. `message_update_with_read_disposition_deleted_serialises_correctly` — same but `Deleted` / `"deleted"`.

3. `message_update_with_read_disposition_processed_serialises_correctly` — same but `Processed` / `"processed"`.

4. `message_update_with_read_disposition_other_serialises_correctly` — same but `Other("voice-listened".into())` / `"voice-listened"`. Asserts the `Other` wire-value round-trip works on the client side just as it does in `jmap-chat-types`.

5. `message_update_without_read_disposition_omits_field` — set `read_at` alone (no `read_disposition`), assert the emitted payload has `"readAt"` but no `"readDisposition"` key. Documents that the server's "default to displayed" behavior is reachable from the client by omitting the field.

Test oracles: hardcoded JSON expectations derived from the spec §Message/set wording — independent of the code under test per workspace test-integrity rules.

## Verification

```bash
cargo fmt --all
cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings
cargo test -p jmap-chat-client
cargo test --workspace
```

## Out of scope

- `MessageCreateInput.read_disposition` — see Implementation sketch §3 above; spec is silent and the bead recommends omitting.
- `Peer/receipt` plumbing — the `DeliveryReceipt` type already has `read_disposition` on the receive (deserialize) side via `jmap-chat-types`; client receiving the field works today. Bead is about settable-on-update only.
- Server-side or chat-types changes (both are already complete).

## History

Spec edit (`bb7ff59`, 2026-05-02) landed `ReadDisposition` in chat-types and chat-server. The chat-client catch-up was missed. Discovered 2026-05-12 during a post-`80d5e11` audit that asked "do the chat sources match the current spec".
title: chat-client: plumb readDisposition through Message/set update binding
